MSC Virtuosa Review

Review of MSC Virtuosa

The 2021-built MSC Virtuosa cruise ship is MSC’s second MERAVIGLIA PLUS-class vessel, with sisterships MSC Grandiosa (2019) and MSC Euribia (2023). Meraviglia Plus vessels are an upgraded and enlarged evolution of the earlier Meraviglia-class ships MSC Meraviglia (2017) and MSC Bellissima (2019).

The vessel (IMO number 9803625) is currently Malta-flagged (MMSI 215610000) and registered in Valletta.

History – construction and ownership

MSC Cruises (MSC Crociere) is a passenger shipping company headquartered in Genoa and Naples. Founded in 1960, today MSC Crociere is part of MSC (Mediterranean Shipping Company) – the world’s 2nd-largest container shipping company. MSC Crociere is the world’s largest privately owned cruise company.

By annual passenger volumes, MSC ranks as the world’s 3rd-largest cruise shipowner, following Carnival Corporation and RCG–Royal Caribbean Group.

Decks and Cabins

MSC Virtuosa staterooms (2421 total, across 17 categories) accommodate a maximum of 6334 passengers (4810 lower berths). Approximately 75% of all cabins feature private step-out balconies. The largest accommodations are the MSC Yacht Club Royal Suites (700 ft2 / 65 m2 plus a 430 ft2 / 40 m2 terrace with Jacuzzi).

The ship has 18 decks (3 crew-only, 15 passenger-accessible, 11 with cabins), and features “cluster cabins” (up to 3 interconnecting staterooms) allowing a maximum capacity of 10 guests. Additional accommodations include 95 Yacht Club Suites (with 24-hour butler service and exclusive facilities), 15 Interior Studios (solo traveler cabins without a single supplement), and 60 ADA-compliant staterooms (wheelchair-accessible).

MSC Virtuosa’s decks are named after the world’s most famous composers.

The vessel has a total service area of 460,000 m2 (4.95 million ft2) and 35,000 m2 (376,736 ft2) of public areas, with a public space ratio of 7.7 m2 (83 ft2) per passenger. Onboard amenities include 4 swimming pools (1 sliding-roof-covered and 1 MSC Yacht Club pool), 9 Jacuzzis, and 32 elevators (19 passenger lifts, including 1 reserved for MSC Yacht Club and 2 panoramic glass-walled Atrium lifts).

Shipboard dining options – Food and Drinks

The ship offers 12 diverse dining venues, including the Mediterranean Village specialty restaurant and the exclusive Yacht Club Fine Dining Restaurant. The Marketplace Buffet is open 20 hours per day and offers international cuisine, Mediterranean specialties, itinerary-themed dishes, healthy selections, and dietary menus. Other fine dining venues include Kaito Sushi Bar, Kaito Teppanyaki, and an American-style steakhouse serving premium cuts from around the world.

Below is the complete list of MSC Virtuosa restaurants and food bars.

  • 5 Main Restaurants (MDRs) serving traditional Italian meals and wines; open for breakfast (7–9:30 am), lunch (12–2 pm), and dinner with two fixed seatings (7 pm and 9:30 pm). A 7-course dinner menu is offered, including vegan and vegetarian options.
  • Blue Danube Restaurant (598 seats; 11,302 ft2 / 1050 m2) – complimentary restaurant with fixed dining times, serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Located aft on Deck 5 behind Reception. Despite its aft location, it has no aft windows, only portholes. Buffet-style service with a la carte options.
  • Sea Pavilion by Jereme Leung (155 seats; 4197 ft2 / 390 m2) – available on China itineraries.
  • Eataly Restaurant – Eataly-branded food market and specialty dining venue.
  • La Piazzetta Restaurant – self-service buffet and pizzeria; offers afternoon tea and occasional midnight buffets.
  • Marketplace Buffet Restaurant & Bar (1336 seats; 39,288 ft2 / 3650 m2), open 6:30 am–10 pm, serving international and Mediterranean dishes, world cuisine, healthy options.
  • MSC Yacht Club Restaurant (4359 ft2 / 405 m2) – open for breakfast, lunch, and dinner with no fixed dining times; menus vary by itinerary.
  • Masters of the Sea (81 seats; 340 m2) – MSC’s classic British-style pub offering 12 beers on tap, 47 bottled varieties, cider, and bar snacks including fish & chips.
  • Kaito Teppanyaki & Sushi Bar – a la carte priced; open 12–2:30 pm and 7–11 pm; three menu tiers (Geisha EUR 18, Samurai EUR 24, Emperor EUR 45).
  • Butcher’s Cut (58 seats; 753 ft2 / 70 m2) – American steakhouse with large cuts, starters, seafood, and signature desserts.
  • Minuetto Restaurant (714 seats; 10,763 ft2 / 1000 m2) – features Flexi and MyTime Dining.
  • The Opera and The Simphony (908 seats; 14,402 ft2 / 1338 m2) – connected MDRs with Enomatic wine stations and Flexi/MyTime dining.
  • Il Campo Restaurant (188 seats; 3584 ft2 / 333 m2).
  • Sports Bar (24 seats; 3433 ft2 / 319 m2) – serves drinks, snacks, hot dogs, popcorn, shakes, juices.
  • Jean-Philippe Maury Chocolaterie – chocolate atelier and creperie offering gourmet ice cream.
  • Champagne Bar – premium sparkling wines with caviar, oysters, crab.
  • Edge Cocktail Bar.
  • (NEW) HOLA! Tacos & Cantina – Latin American/Mexican street-food concept.
  • (NEW) Indochine Restaurant – Vietnamese cuisine “with a French twist”.
 

On Virtuosa, MSC introduced two new specialty dining venues: “HOLA! Tacos & Cantina” and “Ristorante Indochine”.

  • HOLA is a fast-casual venue serving Latin American and Mexican dishes. Signature items include blue corn tacos (including vegetarian options), nachos, empanadas, tamales, and tortilla soup. The salsa bar offers six homemade salsas, spicy sauces, and fresh guacamole.
  • Indochine Restaurant (66 seats; 1108 ft2 / 103 m2) offers Vietnamese specialties with French influences. The menu includes vegetarian/vegan options and family-style dishes for sharing.

Shipboard entertainment options – Fun and Sport

Meraviglia Plus-class ships feature new original productions. A total of eight exclusive shows are available across the Meraviglia and Meraviglia Plus fleets.

 

MSC Virtuosa has a large water park (Savannah Aquapark) connected to a two-level indoor amusement park and a two-deck promenade housing specialty restaurants, bars, and duty-free shops. The promenade is covered by a spectacular LED dome (“digital sky”) displaying dynamic visual shows.

The ship also features advanced wristband technology enabling contactless payments, spa and dining reservations, and geo-location for children.

Below is the full list of MSC Virtuosa lounges, clubs, and entertainment venues for children, teens, and adults.

  • (NEW) L’Atelier Bistrot (148 seats; 3315 ft2 / 308 m2) – bar and art lounge with stage, dance floor, and pop-up gallery.
  • Sky Lounge & Bar (180 seats; 6781 ft2 / 630 m2) – panoramic cocktail lounge with adjacent Cigar Room.

  • Champagne Bar (155 seats; 6393 ft2 / 594 m2).

In 2022, MSC introduced two new Carousel Lounge productions—AJEDREZ and ARKYMEA—developed by “Carousel Productions at Sea”, combining music, lighting, and acrobatic performances.

MSC Starship Club’s Rob – the first humanoid robot bartender at sea

MSC Virtuosa introduced the fleet’s first MSC Starship Club (MSC Starliner One Bar), a futuristic venue featuring the cruise industry’s first humanoid robot bartender, Rob. MSC worked for six years with specialists in robotics, digital solutions, entertainment, and interior design to create this concept.

The Starship Club features 3D holographic projections, a digital art wall, and a 12-seat interactive galactic tour table. Rob prepares and serves cocktails using natural human-like movements and communicates in eight languages. He interacts with guests using gestures, jokes, riddles, and expressive LED facial animations. Drinks are ordered via digital cockpits and served in MSC-branded futuristic souvenir glasses.

Itineraries

MSC Virtuosa’s maiden season in Europe is based on 5 homeports (Barcelona, Genoa, Civitavecchia, Palermo, Marseille) operating 7-day Western Mediterranean roundtrips, with calls in Valletta (Malta).

In mid-January 2021, MSC announced the ship’s deployment in Asia (homeported in China) starting in 2022, joining MSC Bellissima. MSC has offered China-based cruises since 2016 (MSC Lirica), followed by deployments of Splendida (2018) and Bellissima (2021).

In late March 2021, MSC announced Virtuosa’s homeporting in the UK for summer 2021 (starting May 20). The program included 3-4-night roundtrips followed by 7-night itineraries (starting June 12). Short cruises visited the Isle of Portland with two sea days. The 7-night voyages visited Portland and Belfast. Homeports were Liverpool and Greenock–Glasgow.

MSC Virtuosa Wiki

The vessel (STX France, Chantiers de l’Atlantique yard / hull number H34) has a volume of 181,541 GT, a deadweight tonnage of 19,610 tons, and a max draught of 9 m. The powerplant consists of four Wärtsilä marine diesel engines (2x 12V46DF and 2x 16V46DF) with a combined output of 64 MW (85,830 hp). Propulsion is provided by two Azipod thrusters with a combined output of 40 MW (53,640 hp). The registered shipowner is VISTA 4 COMPANIA NAVIERA SA, and the registered manager is MSC CROCIERE SPA.

On February 1, 2016, MSC announced a shipbuilding order for two Meraviglia Plus-class units. The newbuilds have a maximum capacity of 6300 passengers, feature 200 additional cabins, and are 16 m / 50 ft longer than the Meraviglia-class vessels. The Meraviglia Plus-class ships were delivered in October 2019 (Grandiosa) and April 2020 (Virtuosa).

Bookings for MSC Virtuosa cruises opened on November 21, 2018 (for MSC Voyagers Club members), and on December 3 for the general public. Sales for the inaugural voyage (scheduled for November 8, 2020, from Genoa) opened on October 7, 2018. The promotional offer for MSC Voyagers Club members granted exclusive early access (through October 21) and an additional 5% discount, on top of the standard 5% loyalty discount. All customers were eligible for a 5% Early Booking Discount through June 3, 2019.

Construction began with the keel-laying (coin ceremony) on February 27, 2019, at St Nazaire’s Chantiers de l’Atlantique shipyard. The vessel was originally scheduled for delivery in November 2020. On the same day (Feb 27), Bellissima was delivered to MSC. During the traditional ceremony, two shipyard employees placed two special-edition coins beneath the first keel block for good luck. The ceremony’s godmothers were Helen Huang (MSC Cruises China President) and Elise Guerin (shipyard Project Manager).

The vessel was launched (floated out from drydock) on December 1, 2019, following the delivery of MSC Grandiosa (October 31) and the steel-cutting of MSC World Europa (also on October 31). Chantiers de l'Atlantique officially delivered Virtuosa to MSC on February 1, 2021. The ceremony was attended by Pierfrancesco Vago (MSC Executive Chairman) and his family (wife Alexa Aponte-Vago and their children), along with Laurent Castaing (shipyard General Manager).

In mid-July 2021, MSC announced that Virtuosa’s christening ceremony would be held at Port Rashid (Dubai, UAE). The naming event took place on November 27, 2021, as part of the UAE Golden Jubilee celebrations (marking the nation’s 50th anniversary, April 6, 2021–March 31, 2022). The ceremony was attended by MSC’s traditional godmother Sophia Loren (Italian actress, born 1934), who has christened 17 of MSC’s 19 ships since 2003. VIP guests included Pierfrancesco Vago (MSC), Sultan Ahmed Bin Sulayem (DP World President and CEO), His Excellency Helal Saeed Al Marri (Director-General of DTCM/Dubai Tourism), and His Highness Sheikh Mansoor Bin Mohammed Bin Saeed Rashid Al Maktoum (UAE Vice President and Prime Minister).

Meraviglia Plus-class ship technology

New features on Meraviglia Plus-class vessels include the first fine-art museum at sea (displaying original artworks), an extended indoor promenade (Galleria) measuring 111 m / 36 ft, and a larger LED screen (95x6 m / 280x20 ft) for the pool deck’s outdoor theater. The expanded Galleria space accommodates two additional restaurants. MSC established exclusive partnerships with Samsung (providing digital technologies) and Cirque du Soleil (providing live entertainment programming).

Meraviglia Plus-class ships are also the fleet’s most technologically advanced, incorporating next-generation marine engine technologies. Their equipment includes hybrid scrubbers (exhaust gas cleaning systems), SCR (selective catalytic reduction converting NOx into nitrogen), an advanced waste management plant, the latest wastewater treatment systems, enhanced recycling capabilities, and fuel-efficient heat recovery systems.

MSC's ZOE

On February 1, 2019, MSC officially revealed the in-cabin digital assistant ZOE. Developed by Harman International (USA-based, a wholly-owned Samsung subsidiary), ZOE represents a cruise industry first. Harman is known for creating advanced digital audio technologies for major corporations (including Google, Microsoft, Amazon).

ZOE is a voice-enabled artificial intelligence device with advanced voice recognition available in all staterooms. It speaks seven languages, answers cruise-related questions, provides details on shipboard services, activities, and facilities, and assists with reservations and bookings.

The device features far-field microphones, a high-quality speaker, a quad-core processor (ensuring fast response times), and direct phone connectivity via Bluetooth. The system can upgrade its own database to answer newly emerging questions.

Passenger data (including itineraries, tours, and onboard preferences) is stored in a cloud-based system and reused on subsequent voyages.

The device (approx. 15 cm tall) can be activated at any time. Passengers must sign a waiver authorizing the storage of their personal data.

 

Beginning with MSC Bellissima (2019), ZOE is available on all newbuild MSC ships and is being introduced fleetwide from 2019 through 2024.

Inaugural cruise itineraries 2021

MSC Virtuosa was eventually rescheduled to enter service on April 16, launching a short inaugural season in the Mediterranean (4 voyages / 3-, 4-, and 10-night itineraries) before repositioning from the Mediterranean to the Baltic for deployment in Germany. The Northern Europe program (roundtrips from Kiel) began on May 8, offering 7-day and 14-day B2B voyages.
